From: Rachel Stone <rachel.stone@meditech.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial RFI: offline/orchestration and segmentation requirements

Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this—Meditech is evaluating vendors for a fully isolated on-prem deployment (air-gapped option). We have a compact set of technical questions the engineering and security teams want to validate before we move to a POC. High-level ask: can you provide concise answers (plus any supporting runbooks/diagrams) on the items below? Where applicable, note constraints for a "strictly offline" install.

1) Orchestration model: Do you require a central controller that phones home, or can your runtime be completely controller-less?
2) Network segmentation: recommended L4/L7 boundaries; support for outbound-only egress via jump-host; firewall rule examples.
3) Offline updates: artifact format, signing model, how to push patches into air-gapped clusters.
4) Image provenance: how do you provide SBOM, signed images, and reproducible build hashes?
5) Configuration management: supported secret stores (KMS/HSM); rotation workflows when no external KMS is allowed.
6) Operational access: debug workflows for triage without opening inbound access; audit log export.

We'd like answers by next Friday so our infra team can schedule a 1-hour technical deep-dive. If you have a short one-page architecture sketch and an update playbook stub, please attach.

Thanks,
Rachel Stone
Head of Infrastructure Security
Meditech Health Systems

[Attachment: meditech-rfi-20260610.xlsx]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Rachel Stone <rachel.stone@meditech.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial RFI: offline/orchestration and segmentation requirements

Rachel—

Appreciate the clear list. I've summarized our capabilities below and attached two artifacts: an isolation architecture sketch and a concise airgap update playbook. Where you note "strictly offline", I've called out the offline-specific steps. If anything needs deeper detail we can bring engineers to the call.

1) Orchestration model
- Redwood Private supports both: a controller-mode (management plane) and a fully controller-less option for locked-down installations.
- Controller-less mode: each node runs the Redwood Private Agent (RPA) that performs local decisioning; rollouts are coordinated via signed artifact bundles you push to an internal registry; no outbound connection is required once artifacts are staged.

2) Network segmentation
- Recommended boundaries: management plane (if used) in a control VLAN; inference GPUs in a compute VLAN; storage in a separate CIFS/NFS VLAN.
- For air-gapped installs we support an outbound-only egress tunnel via a dedicated jump-host for controlled artifact pulls. Example firewall rules in attached sketch (allow TCP 443/8443 outbound from jump-host only; block inbound to compute VLAN).

3) Offline updates
- Artifact format: gzipped tarball with metadata.json and signed_manifest.sig.
- Signing: we sign with an RFC 8037-compatible key. Customers may verify signatures locally; we provide verification tooling.
- Update flow (offline): stage artifact on USB or internal registry -> validate signature & hash -> deploy via agent using local rollout policy. Playbook shows step-by-step.

4) Image provenance
- We provide SBOMs per artifact (CycloneDX JSON) and reproducible build instructions. Images are signed using in-house signing; we can provide detached signature files and SHA512 hashes.

5) Configuration & secrets
- Supported key stores: customer-managed HSM, Vault, and KMIP-compatible appliances. For fully offline deployments we offer a sealed-secret key workflow: admin imports encrypted key bundles via the offline channel; local HSM recommended.

6) Operational access & auditing
- Debug/troubleshoot: agent-side logs can be exported to an internal log collector; for emergency triage we support time-limited ephemeral session tokens brokered via a jump-host (no inbound firewall changes).
- Audit logs: runbook describes exporting signed audit bundles for external review.

Next steps
- I've attached: isolation-architecture-sketch.pdf and airgap-update-playbook_v1.pdf.
- Proposed deep-dive: Tue 2026-06-15 10:00 PT. I'll send a calendar invite if that works.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: isolation-architecture-sketch.pdf (diagram), airgap-update-playbook_v1.pdf (playbook)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: technical clarifications and port/evidence examples

Rachel, quick technical follow-up after today's call (thanks everyone for the time). A few specifics that your infra team asked for:

- Ports/protocols: inbound to jump-host only for admin (SSH/TLS) blocked by default; outbound allowed from jump-host to internal registry over TLS 443 or 8443. Compute nodes only require outbound DNS + NTP when live; in full airgap mode, both DNS/NTP can be served internally.
- Container runtime: we support containerd and CRI-O for runtime; OCI images with signed manifests preferred.
- Offline registry: we supply tooling to generate a tarball of the registry snapshot with content hashes and a registry-metadata.json to import into an internal registry appliance.
- Bootstrap artifacts: our boot bundle includes: redwood-agent binary (sha512: 3a7f...), runtime libs, SBOM.json, and signed_manifest.sig.

Evidence we can share (redacted for public docs): sample SBOM, a signed image manifest, and a short attestation doc for image signing processes. Attestation will be provided as a DOCX that your legal team can review.

Let us know if you need additional low-level examples (e.g., sample iptables rules or a sample registry import command).

Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: sample-sbom-cyclonedx.json (redacted)]
